newsitem.title: USA: Toll Brothers had record Q4 revenues.
newsitem.headline: Toll Brothers had record Q4 revenues.

text.p: Toll Brothers Inc said Wednesday it had record revenues and contracts in both its fourth quarter and year ended Oct 31.
The company also said year-end backlog was at a record level for the fifth consecutive year.
Fiscal 1996 revenues from housing sales were some $759.0 million for 2,109 homes, an 18 percent increase over 1995's $643.0 million for 1,825 homes, Toll said.
This was the company's fifth consecutive year of record revenues, it said.

Fourth-quarter revenues from housing sales of some $259.8 million for 718 homes were an all-time single quarter record and were 31 percent above 1995's fourth quarter housing sales revenues of $198.0 million for 555 homes.
For fiscal 1996, the company said, it signed contracts totaling some $884.4 million for 2,398 homes, a 34 percent increase over the previous record, set in 1995, of $660.4 million for 1,846 homes.
This was the company's sixth consecutive year of record contracts, it said.

During its fourth quarter, the company signed contracts totalling about $231.2 million for 603 homes, exceeding by 20 percent the previous fourth quarter record of $192.7 million for 543 homes set in 1995, Toll said.
This marked the 23rd consecutive quarter in which the company has set a quarter-to-quarter record for new sales contracts, it said.
The company's backlog of some $526.2 million for 1,367 homes at Oct 31 surpassed by 31 percent the previous year-end high of $400.8 million for 1,078 homes a year earlier.
"We are riding the crest of a growing wave of affluent baby boomers that we believe will continue to gain momentum well into the next century," Toll said.

"Although the move-up luxury buyer remains our primary customer, our expansion into the empty nester market is already yielding results. In fiscal 1996 roughly 20 percent of our homes were bought by 50-plus-aged households.

"We are also enjoying the benefits of our expanding presence in key southeastern, southwestern and western markets. The communities in our newest markets, California, Arizona, Texas, Florida and North Carolina, contributed approximately $103.6 million (270 homes) to our record year-end backlog," it said. "The market's continued strength, combined with our record backlog and increasing presence in high growth markets, gives us great hope that 1997 will be another excellent year."
